rubrics.justification: Describes a generally good-quality blastocyst with plausible comments on blastocoel, ICM, and TE, but notes uncertainty and possible stage discrepancy; some image-specific details appear speculative.

Integrates maternal age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometrium, male factor, partner age, and first-cycle status well, though interaction between semen findings and embryo competence could be more tightly framed.
Overall logic is clear and probability estimates are tied to morphology, age, and untested status; minor inconsistency remains around exact expansion stage interpretation.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice, including SET preference for a good-quality day-5 blastocyst and cautious discussion of PGT-A; slight looseness around Gardner stage terminology prevents a top score.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and future planning, including SET, luteal support, no bed rest, and consideration of sperm DNA fragmentation/PGT-A if needed, though some advice remains somewhat general.
